acme_sre: Hey team, hitting intermittent structured-output parse failures after we switched to redwood-07b-instruct. ~10% of responses fail schema validation with type issues (numbers/booleans as strings) and enum casing mismatches. Request id r-0a9f1234 included below. Can you advise repro steps or a workaround?

acme_sre: Repro (minimal): POST /v1/generate json_mode=structured schema= { \"type\": \"object\", \"properties\": { \"count\": {\"type\": \"integer\"}, \"is_active\": {\"type\": \"boolean\"}, \"status\": {\"type\": \"string\", \"enum\": [\"ACTIVE\", \"INACTIVE\"] } }, \"required\": [\"count\",\"is_active\",\"status\"] }

acme_sre: Example model output we received (raw):
```json
{
  \"count\": \"42\",
  \"is_active\": \"true\",
  \"status\": \"active\"
}
```

acme_sre: Parser error at server: structured_output_parse_error: type_mismatch(count expected integer got string) -> thrown at parse stage 2. Occurs across regions.

maya_support: Thanks for the reproduction — sorry about the disruption. Can you confirm the model name + exact request_id and timestamp for the failing call? Also are you routing through Dedicated or Hosted? :eyes:

acme_sre: model=redwood-07b-instruct, request_id=r-0a9f1234, ts=1784009800 UTC. We're on Hosted API (no Dedicated pool). Happening in eu-west and us-east.

support-bot: [ingest] request_id=r-0a9f1234, model=redwood-07b-instruct, node=hosted-12, parse_error=type_mismatch(count:string->integer)

devon_engineer: Quick notes: LLMs sometimes emit numbers/booleans as strings when the prompt doesn't strongly enforce type tokens, and enums can be lowercased depending on temperature/decoding. Two short-term mitigations: 1) strengthen the system prompt to explicitly state required JSON types and show canonical examples, 2) apply a deterministic post-parse coercion map on your side for enums/booleans/numbers.

devon_engineer: Example system prompt tweak: \"You must output valid JSON matching the schema. Numbers must be unquoted (e.g. 42), booleans must be plain true/false, and enums must use exact casing (ACTIVE or INACTIVE). If uncertain, prefer the enum exact token.\"

ops-lucas: We can also flip a temporary server-side fallback: enable enum_case_coercion + lax_number_coerce for that org for 24h while we investigate. It will attempt to coerce \"true\"->true, \"42\"->42 and map \"active\"->\"ACTIVE\" before final schema validation. Want me to enable? :thumbsup:

acme_sre: Yes please enable it for 24h while we roll a fix. That reduced failures in our quick smoke to ~2% from 10%. Thanks.

maya_support: Done — enabled enum_case_coercion=true and lax_number_coerce=true for acme (org-id: org-452). I created ticket SUP-2026-118 to track. We'll need engineering to root-cause (model template / decoding steering).

devon_engineer: For a durable fix we should: 1) add stronger few-shot examples in the model's structured-output template, 2) lower sampling (temp) or use constrained decoding for enum tokens, 3) add server-side canonicalization fallback for known enum fields. I'll open ENG-ML ticket and link SUP-2026-118.

acme_sre: Appreciate that. One more oddity — sometimes nulls come back as the string \"null\" which still slips through coercion. Any ideas?

devon_engineer: For nulls, we treat literal token \"null\" as ambiguous. We can add explicit rule: if schema allows null, accept string \"null\" -> null; otherwise flag for manual review. I'll add to the ENG-ML ticket.

maya_support: Escalation steps: we've logged SUP-2026-118, assigned to devon_engineer (owner), target triage ETA 24h. For now your temporary coercion is active. We'll follow up with a patch plan. :white_check_mark:

acme_sre: Great thank you — will monitor and report back if anything else pops up.

ops-lucas: FYI I've attached the live parse logs to SUP-2026-118 and set a 24h rollback window for the coercion flags.

acme_sre: Confirmed — failures dropped and we can proceed with the change. Thanks everyone. :pray:
